# Dashboard Starter

## Where this fits

This dashboard adapts the Week 7 descriptive summary into a dashboard-style
KT product. It uses one editable control value, one visualization, one table,
one interpretation, and one caution — the 1-1-1-1-1 rule made concrete.

## Goal

This dashboard helps community health workers working on a nutrition project
use a plain-language overview of descriptive BMI patterns in the classroom
NHANES equity dataset as context for their work.

## Audience Question

Audience: community health workers working on a nutrition project who need a
plain-language overview of BMI patterns.

Question: among adults age 20-80, how does mean BMI vary across NHANES cycles
for one selected income group?

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)

data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Control

In a Shiny app, this would become a dropdown. In this static dashboard, change
the value of `selected_income` and render again to update the table and chart.

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-control
available_income_groups <- sort(unique(na.omit(nhanes$IncomeGroup)))
selected_income <- "Low Income (<1.3)"

if (!selected_income %in% available_income_groups) {
  selected_income <- available_income_groups[1]
}

selected_income
```

For comparison, other valid values in the classroom dataset are
`"Middle Income"` and `"High Income (>3.5)"`. Copy a value exactly,
including the quotes and any parentheses.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-summary
dashboard_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(
    Age >= 20,
    Age <= 80,
    IncomeGroup == selected_income,
    !is.na(BMI),
    !is.na(Cycle)
  ) |>
  group_by(Cycle) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(dashboard_summary)
```

## Visualization

```{r}
#| label: dashboard-plot
ggplot(dashboard_summary, aes(x = Cycle, y = mean_bmi)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2f6f73") +
  labs(
    title = paste("Mean BMI for", selected_income),
    subtitle = "Adults age 20-80 in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom dataset",
    x = "NHANES cycle",
    y = "Mean BMI",
    caption = "Descriptive, unweighted classroom summary. Missing BMI, income group, cycle, and out-of-cohort ages are excluded."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

## Interpretation

For the selected income group, the table and bar chart describe mean BMI
across available NHANES cycles among adults age 20-80 in the prepared
classroom dataset. This comparison can provide context for a nutrition
project; it does not explain why the values differ or measure project impact.
BMI alone is not a comprehensive measure of nutrition or health.

## Limitation

The BMI patterns are descriptive, not causal: they do not show that income
causes BMI differences or that a nutrition project changed BMI.

## Testing

Before submitting a dashboard-style product:

1. Render this page from the repository root.
2. Change `selected_income` to another value from `available_income_groups`.
3. Render again and check that the table, title, and plot all update.
4. Verify that the caption still names the dataset, exclusions, and limitation.
5. Record any warning or error in your testing log.

From the repository root, render the submitted copy with:

```bash
quarto render assignments/assignment07-dashboard/submission/dashboard.qmd
```

HTML is the expected output for this dashboard — you do not need a PDF. If the
render log warns about a missing TeX installation or a PDF problem, you can
ignore it as long as the `.html` file was created. The Week 8 course page walks
through the full six-step test routine.

## Privacy-Safe Publishing

- Use aggregate summaries, not row-level records.
- Avoid small-cell interpretations when `n` is low.
- State that outputs are descriptive and unweighted.
- Keep cached classroom data separate from any raw NHANES retrieval workflow.
- Do not upload row-level data to external AI tools.
